framework: ISO/IEC TR 24027:2021 Information technology - Artificial intelligence (AI) - Bias in AI systems and AI aided decision making
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue page says the report describes measurement techniques and methods for assessing bias, with all AI system lifecycle phases in scope, including testing, evaluation and use.
what_is_tested: Bias in AI systems and AI aided decision making

framework: ETSI EN 304 223 V2.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Recommended: use independent security testers with technical skills relevant to the AI system; share testing findings with System Operators; and evaluate model outputs so that they do not let operators or end users reverse engineer the model or gain unintended influence over the system.
what_is_tested: Security assessment findings and model outputs
who_tests: Independent security testers; Developers; System Operators

framework: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019, amended 8 Nov 2023 and 3 May 2024 as read
requirement_paraphrase: Governments should consider using experimentation to provide a controlled environment in which AI systems can be tested, and scaled up as appropriate.
what_is_tested: AI systems in controlled experimentation environments

framework: International AI Safety Report, Second Key Update: Technical Safeguards and Risk Management (25 November 2025)
clause_or_page: Section 1 Introduction, para. 2 (no page numbers in text read)
requirement_paraphrase: Reports that three leading developers applied enhanced safeguards to new models because their internal pre deployment testing could not rule out possible help with biological weapons misuse (wording seen: 'could not rule out').
what_is_tested: Biological misuse uplift (dangerous capability), internal pre deployment testing

framework: MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1, Guidance on Qualification and Classification of Software in Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR), revised June 2025
clause_or_page: Section 8 (Consideration of changes to an MDSW), p. 25
requirement_paraphrase: Safety and performance are to be ensured through a continuous process of clinical and/or performance evaluation and risk management, and the effect of changes to function, intended use, design and manufacturing on qualification and classification must be evaluated.
what_is_tested: Medical device software safety and performance over its lifecycle

framework: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I (FAA; issue date not stated in the text read)
clause_or_page: Section 'Assuring the Safety of AI', p. 20
requirement_paraphrase: States that validation of a learned AI system needs supplemental guidance, asking how to show a learned model performs as expected, and proposes treating the model as a mathematical function while treating its implementation as traditional engineering.
what_is_tested: Learned (design time fixed) AI model verification and validation
who_tests: Applicants and the FAA (certification framework to be developed)

framework: SR 11-7, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (dated 4 April 2011, last updated 19 August 2011 per page)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation covers evaluation of conceptual soundness (design, construction, documentation, empirical support), ongoing monitoring to confirm the model performs as intended, and outcomes analysis comparing model outputs with actual outcomes, including back-testing.
what_is_tested: Model design quality, in-use performance and agreement of outputs with realised outcomes

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Regularly assess AI functions and test their resilience through offensive security exercises (red teaming), and continuously validate and refine AI models in simulated environments before deployment.
what_is_tested: AI resilience to attack; model behaviour in simulation

framework: MHRA, Software and AI as a Medical Device Change Programme roadmap (GOV.UK guidance; visible date 'Updated 14 June 2023')
clause_or_page: WP 3 Premarket requirements, objective 1 and items WP3-01 and WP3-02
requirement_paraphrase: Planned work to ensure software as a medical device is supported by adequate data on safety, effectiveness and quality, including a review of essential requirements (secondary legislation) and best practice development and deployment guidance.
what_is_tested: Premarket evidence of safety, effectiveness and quality of software including AI

framework: FCA press release: FCA set to launch Live AI Testing service (first published 29/04/2025, last updated 05/12/2025)
clause_or_page: Press release body; no clause numbers
requirement_paraphrase: The FCA describes a service, proposed at the time of the release, where firms ready to deploy consumer or market facing AI models work with the FCA to check new AI tools are ready to be used.
what_is_tested: Readiness of consumer or market facing AI tools before deployment (criteria not specified)

framework: AI Discussion Paper (AIディスカッションペーパー) version 1.0, Financial Services Agency, March 2025 (summary PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: States that for generative AI there are no established systematic performance metrics, so development, operation and management structures are still being built.
what_is_tested: Performance evaluation of generative AI (metrics gap)

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluation should cover the variations expected in clinical use (for example imaging conditions, patient population, lesion location, facility, realistic prevalence) to confirm there is no evident weakness; the slide says it is hard to explain objectively that coverage is comprehensive.
what_is_tested: Coverage of variation in evaluation data

framework: Consumer Protection in respect of Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence, HKMA circular dated 19 August 2024 (as stated in the fetched text)
requirement_paraphrase: Authorised institutions should ensure proper validation of generative AI models is in place and, early in deploying customer facing applications, keep a human in the loop over decisions.
what_is_tested: Validation of generative AI models for customer facing use
